title: How to Replace an HVAC UV Light Bulb, Step by Step
h1: How Do You Replace an HVAC UV Light Bulb?
description: Step-by-step guide to replacing the UV bulb in your HVAC system safely: when to change it, how to handle the lamp, and the mistakes that shorten its life.
quick_answer: Turn off power to the UV light and the HVAC system, let the lamp cool, then remove the old bulb from its housing without touching the new bulb's glass. Slide in the matching replacement, reconnect it, restore power and confirm it's glowing through the viewing port. Most UV bulbs need replacing about once a year.
body:
How often does an HVAC UV bulb need replacing?

Most manufacturers call for a new bulb about every 12 months, even if it still glows. UV lamps lose germicidal strength over time, so a bulb that looks fine may not be doing much anymore. Check your unit's manual or the label on the housing for the exact interval and bulb model.

Many homeowners tie the bulb change to their yearly AC tune-up in spring so it's easy to remember. If your unit has an indicator light or a lamp-life timer, that will also tell you when it's due.

What do you need before you start?

  • The correct replacement bulb. Match the model number from the old lamp or the housing, not just the length.
  • Clean cotton or nitrile gloves, or a lint-free cloth, for handling the new bulb.
  • A flashlight, since UV units are often in a dark attic, closet or garage.
  • A container or bag to hold the old bulb safely.

Most HVAC UV lamps are installed through the side of the duct or the air handler, near the indoor coil. In San Diego homes that often means a hall closet, the garage or the attic.

How do you replace the bulb safely?

  1. Shut off the power. Turn the thermostat off, then switch off the UV unit and, if it's wired to the air handler, the air handler's service switch or breaker. Never look at a lit UV lamp. UV-C light can burn your eyes and skin.
  2. Let it cool. Give the lamp a few minutes to cool down before handling it.
  3. Disconnect the lamp. Many units have a twist-lock or a small connector at the base. Release it and gently pull the bulb straight out of the housing. Don't force it, since the glass is thin.
  4. Handle the new bulb by its base. Wear gloves or use a clean cloth. Oils from your fingers leave spots on the glass that block UV output and can shorten the bulb's life.
  5. Install the new bulb. Slide it into the housing the same way the old one came out and lock it in place. Reconnect the power connector.
  6. Restore power and check. Turn the unit and the system back on. Most housings have a small viewing window or indicator that shows the lamp is lit. Look at the indicator, not at the lamp itself.

If you need to open a panel that exposes wiring, or the unit is hardwired into the air handler and you aren't sure what's live, stop there and have a technician do it. Electrical internals aren't a DIY job.

What should you do with the old bulb?

Many UV lamps contain a small amount of mercury, like fluorescent tubes. Don't toss them in the household trash. Put the old bulb in the replacement's box or a sealed bag and take it to a household hazardous waste drop-off. San Diego County and Orange County both have collection options for fluorescent and mercury-containing lamps.

If a bulb breaks, air out the area, avoid vacuuming the pieces, and carefully collect the fragments with stiff paper and tape before sealing them in a bag.

What mistakes shorten a UV bulb's life?

  • Touching the glass with bare hands.
  • Buying a bulb that fits but isn't rated for your ballast.
  • Leaving a dead or weak bulb in place for years. It looks like you have UV protection when you don't.
  • Skipping a quick wipe of the sleeve or glass. Dust buildup blocks UV output, so give it a gentle wipe with a dry, lint-free cloth when you change the bulb.

When should you call a technician instead?

Call for help if the new bulb won't light, the unit trips a breaker, you see scorched wiring, or the housing is in a spot you can't reach safely. A tech can also check whether the lamp is aimed where it does the most good, which is usually the indoor coil and drain pan.

We service and install UV lights as part of our indoor air quality work, and we can swap the bulb during a regular tune-up so it's one less thing to track.
faqs: Can I use any UV bulb that fits my HVAC unit?

No. Use the bulb model listed for your specific UV unit. Bulbs that look alike can have different wattage, connectors or ballast requirements. A mismatched bulb may not light, may burn out quickly, or may not put out the intended UV strength.
Is it safe to look at an HVAC UV light to see if it works?

No. UV-C light can hurt your eyes and skin, even from a short glance. Use the viewing port or indicator light on the housing to confirm it's on. Always switch the unit off before opening the housing or removing the bulb.
My UV bulb still glows. Do I still need to replace it?
Usually, yes. UV bulbs keep glowing long after their germicidal output drops. Most manufacturers recommend replacing them about once a year, whether or not they still light up.
Does the UV light run all the time?

Most coil UV lights are designed to run continuously, so they keep the coil and drain pan clean even when the system is idle. Some models switch on only with the blower. Your unit's manual will say which type you have.
